_README: Deployment profiles. One profile = one trained head set + the calibration
fitted FOR those heads. They travel together and must never be mixed: a
Platt mapping describes one model, so serving profile X's heads under
profile Y's calibration produces confident numbers that mean nothing.
An explicit VERICALL_CALIB_DIR / VERICALL_CKPT_A / VERICALL_CKPT_A2 still
wins over the profile, so existing setups are unaffected.
TO ADD A LANGUAGE: build the paired corpus, train, fit calibration, then
add an entry here. No code change is required -- see
calibration profile exists, because an uncalibrated head cannot produce
a trustworthy likelihood ratio and the gateway will refuse to serve it.

baseline.note: The original heads. Scores 42.29% on Hindi -- do not use it for Indian languages.

rtc.note: Trained on transmitted audio. Removed the Mandarin score inversion.

hindi-clean.note: Better on clean audio and has NO telephony bucket: a G.711 call falls back to a wideband mapping. Use hindi-telephony unless the audio really is clean.

hindi-telephony.note: The demo default. Calibrated per channel, so a telephone call is scored by a mapping fitted on telephone audio.

indic5.display: Five Indian languages, pooled (NOT SERVABLE YET)
indic5.note: The head is trained and measured -- including 6.85% on Gujarati, a language it never saw. It is NOT servable: no calibration profile has been fitted for it and there is no A2 counterpart, so it has no likelihood-ratio scale. Fitting those is the next step, and the corpora it needs were lost to a namespace wipe. This entry exists so the slot is defined.
